statement: Let f be a real homogeneous polynomial of degree 2n-3 on R^(n+1). If the real lines on Z(f) in RP^n form a finite set, the sum of their multiplicities as isolated zeros of the restriction section of Sym^(2n-3)(U*) is at least (2n-3)!!. Transversality is not assumed; when all zeros are regular this gives the same lower bound for the ordinary number of real lines.

answer.text: Let f be a real homogeneous polynomial of degree 2n-3 on R^(n+1). If the real lines on Z(f) in RP^n form a finite set, the sum of their multiplicities as isolated zeros of the restriction section of Sym^(2n-3)(U*) is at least (2n-3)!!. Transversality is not assumed; when all zeros are regular this gives the same lower bound for the ordinary number of real lines.

scope: Real hypersurfaces of degree 2n-3 in RP^n with finitely many real lines; multiplicities allowed.
notes: At a nontransverse fibre this is a multiplicity-weighted bound; for simple lines it bounds the ordinary real count.
